chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about hiring out (ijarah), so he said: 'It is good, there is no problem with it if he fulfills his capacity. Musa (peace be upon him) hired out himself and stipulated, saying: 'If you wish, eight (years), and if you wish, ten (years)'. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed regarding it: "You should serve me for eight years; but if you complete ten, it will be of your own free will."'

key_terms.فَمِنْ عِنْدِكَ: It is from you / of your own free will

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on hiring out one's self or services (Ijarah)?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi validates the contract of ijarah by citing the precedent of Prophet Musa (AS), who negotiated a fixed-term service with Prophet Shu'ayb (AS) under the condition of 'if you complete ten, it is from you,' establishing the principle of conditional stipulations in employment. In Shia jurisprudence, this serves as a primary textual proof for the validity of specifying duration and compensation terms, emphasizing that such contracts are permissible provided the servant fulfills their duties with sincerity ('nasaha').
